## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Protocol call (3/4 wells) and conclusion agree on Kinase inhibitors. The atlas neighbours most strongly support this class, with only 1/4 wells voting Microtubule stabilizers, though the strongest single match (10 µM, 0.537) favours stabilizers and the kinase-well similarities are modest (0.36-0.49), so the 0.40 probability is appropriately cautious versus Actin disruptors (0.25) and Microtubule stabilizers (0.20). The phenotype at 10 µM is visually actin-like and actin/tubulin textures rise dose-dependently, but no actin class appears in the atlas neighbours, so that signal is better explained as a shared cytoskeletal consequence of the leading class than as a separate call. The dose selection (0.3-10 µM) correctly tested dose-dependence, each dose is a single replicate but the monotonic trends in actin (rho=+1.00) and tubulin (rho=+1.00) texture across four doses reduce single-well concern. Budget is exhausted (0 left), and a free phenotype on an already-acquired well would not change the NSC vote.

## Unblinding

Compound: **bryostatin** (PubChem CID [6435419](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6435419))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (3/4). The Scientist's own call was **Kinase inhibitors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The Kinase inhibitors call at p=0.40 was correct because I deferred to the e9 NSC majority (3/4 wells at 0.3, 1 and 3 uM) rather than the single 10 uM outlier in e2 that voted Microtubule stabilizers with similarity 0.537. The dose-dependent rises in act_glcm_contrast (rho=+1.00 in e10) and tub_glcm_contrast (rho=+1.00 in e11) replicated in e8 at 3 uM, arguing the cytoskeletal texture was a consistent compound effect, but the absence of any actin class among atlas neighbours kept it as a shared downstream consequence.

I initially overweighted the e4 microscopist Actin disruptors call and the extreme e2 z-scores (act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3) in e6 hypotheses, and the strongest single-well stabilizer match briefly anchored alternatives toward cytoskeletal MoAs. Single-replicate acquisition from 0.3-10 uM left the modest kinase similarities (0.361, 0.485, 0.38) vulnerable to over-interpretation, which is why retaining Actin disruptors 0.25 and Microtubule stabilizers 0.20 was appropriately cautious.

Unblinding to bryostatin clarifies the biology: direct PKC binding (PMID 2001329) with downstream PKD1 and PKC-dependent signaling (PMID 18765827) (PMID 40378651) bins as Kinase inhibitors in the NSC atlas even though the imaged phenotype is actin-like, and the e18 zero-hit actin search shows why no direct bryostatin-actin literature was found.

What was right:
- Trusted e9 NSC 3/4 majority for Kinase inhibitors over the single high-dose Microtubule stabilizers vote at 10 uM
- Treated extreme e2 and e8 actin/tubulin texture z-scores as dose-dependent shared cytoskeletal consequence shown by e10 and e11 rho=+1.00 rather than direct actin disruption
- Kept final probability cautious at 0.40 given modest kinase similarities 0.361-0.485 versus 0.537 stabilizer match

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted e4 visual Actin disruptors call and e2 act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 in early e6 hypotheses with Actin 0.35 versus Kinase 0.15
- Gave too much weight to the strongest single-well 10 uM Microtubule stabilizers match before seeing replication of kinase votes at 0.3, 1 and 3 uM
- Acquired only single replicates at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM with no PKC-specific readout, so could not distinguish PKC modulation from generic kinase inhibition during the blinded run

Proposed next experiment: Treat cells with 1-3 uM bryostatin versus phorbol ester and a PKC-inhibitor co-treatment control, then quantify PKC membrane translocation and PKD1 phosphorylation alongside actin texture and cell solidity with washout to test whether the actin-like phenotype is PKC-dependent.
